summary: CAISO files tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in a new docket, ER27-506-000, as its response to the show cause order. It defines a large load as 50 MW or more, makes generators disclose plans to serve co-located load, and adds a Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) service. Deposits, security and cost recovery sit in the transmission owners' own tariffs, filed separately the same day.
ask: Accept the revisions effective February 16, 2027, with scheduling coordinator changes on November 1, 2027 and settlement changes on April 30, 2028, and set a 30-day comment period.

points.point: A large load is a single site of 50 MW or more.
points.quote: and that has a peak load of 50 MW or greater.

points.point: Deposits, security and cost recovery are left to each transmission owner's tariff.
points.quote: the PTOs will implement just and reasonable deposit, security, reimbursement, and cost-recovery provisions in their own tariffs

points.point: Generator interconnection customers must disclose plans to serve co-located load.
points.quote: requires generator interconnection customers to disclose plans to serve co- located load

points.point: FILI would let flexible loads energize before network upgrades are finished.
points.quote: The CAISO’s Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) can permit earlier energization while network upgrades are pending

points.point: A permanent flexible service is left for later work.
points.quote: with additional work planned on permanent flexibility and other emerging configurations

points.point: CAISO does not require large loads to bring their own generation, and says it will not copy generation-linked mechanisms used in other regions.
points.quote: This distinction also explains why the CAISO does not propose to replicate generation-linked mechanisms developed or proposed in other ISO/RTO regions.

points.point: CAISO says a load sitting near generation does not by itself reduce transmission needs or resource adequacy obligations.
points.quote: physical proximity between load and generation does not guarantee reduced transmission requirements or resource adequacy obligations

points.point: Large loads with backup or non-exporting behind-the-meter generation would be handled under local retail interconnection rules, not CAISO's resource process.
points.quote: These will include large loads with back-up generation only to be used during outages or islanding, and large loads with non-exporting behind-the-meter generation.

points.point: CAISO says it will set out the alternatives, including alternative transmission technologies, considered for each preferred transmission solution.
points.quote: The CAISO will continue to set out the alternatives that were considered in the selection of all preferred transmission solutions, whether ATTs or other more conventional solutions

points.point: CAISO agrees to post cost data for large-load network upgrades on its website in a searchable format.
points.quote: The CAISO agrees that cost data should be transparent and can be provided on the CAISO website in a searchable format.

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-10 show cause order for CAISO. The California transmission owners filed their own tariff revisions in separate dockets the same day.

figures.label: Large load threshold
figures.quote: peak load of 50 MW or greater
